definitions.explanation: A proposal to change or modify an existing plan, bill, or document. Used in legislative, business, and general contexts when suggesting changes to something already drafted.

examples.japanese: {修正案|しゅうせいあん}が{提出|ていしゅつ}された。
{修正案|しゅうせいあん}について{議論|ぎろん}しましょう。
{野党|やとう}が{予算|よさん}の{修正案|しゅうせいあん}を{国会|こっかい}に{提出|ていしゅつ}した。
examples.english: The opposition party submitted a budget amendment to the Diet.

notes:
A compound of {修正|しゅうせい} (correction, revision) and {案|あん} (plan, proposal). Used widely in political, business, and everyday contexts to refer to a proposed change to an existing plan or document.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {修正案|しゅうせいあん}を{出|だ}す: to put forward an amendment
- {修正案|しゅうせいあん}を{提出|ていしゅつ}する: to submit an amendment (formal)
- {修正案|しゅうせいあん}を{可決|かけつ}する: to pass an amendment
- {修正案|しゅうせいあん}を{否決|ひけつ}する: to reject an amendment

USAGE:
In the Japanese Diet ({国会|こっかい}), {修正案|しゅうせいあん} refers specifically to amendments to bills. In business, it can mean any revised draft or plan.

RELATED WORDS:
- {原案|げんあん}: original proposal — the plan before amendment
- {対案|たいあん}: counterproposal — a completely alternative plan
- {改正案|かいせいあん}: reform bill — similar but implies larger-scale change to existing law
